title: Signing a Reconstruction Contract: Tier Entry Gates, Funding and the Contract Sum Line
content:
**Rule.** A Reconstruction contract must be in proposed status when it is signed or declined. The tier is fixed from the property type, the customer type and the contract amount in each tier's entry gate. The contract is signed by the property owner, or by the owner's agent such as the managing property manager or the association's authorized officer; the signature is the customer's own act, and the place of signing is recorded because it decides the cooling-off right. On signing, the contract price is booked to the contract as one contract sum line. An insurance-claim contract must be linked to a claim file of the same customer that is not denied or withdrawn; otherwise the contract is self-pay. A proposal the customer declines, or does not sign, is cancelled with nothing billed.

## Tier entry gates

| Agreement | Property types | Customer types | Contract amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repair Agreement - Minor Repairs | single-family home, condo unit, multifamily unit | any | $500.00 to $9,999.99 |
| Standard Rebuild Agreement | single-family home, condo unit | any | $10,000.00 to $49,999.99 |
| Major Rebuild Agreement | single-family home, condo unit | any | $50,000.00 to $149,999.99 |
| Full Structural Rebuild Agreement | single-family home | any | $150,000.00 or more |
| Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement | multifamily unit | landlord, property manager, association | $10,000.00 or more |
| Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement | commercial property | commercial owner, property manager, association | $10,000.00 or more |

"Any" means the entry gate names no customer type.

## Signing, declining and lapsing

| Event | Contract status required | Who acts | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| The customer signs | proposed | the customer (owner or owner's agent) | the contract is signed; the place of signing (the customer's home, the company office or a remote electronic signature) is recorded; the contract price is booked as one contract sum line dated the signing date |
| The customer declines | proposed | recorded by the desk | the proposal is cancelled; nothing is billed |
| The proposal lapses unsigned | proposed | recorded by the desk | the proposal is cancelled; nothing is billed |

The status test rests on the contract record, read before the action, for the contract being signed or declined.

## Funding source

- **Insurance claim**: the contract is linked to a claim file of the same customer, and that file is not denied or withdrawn.
- **Self-pay**: every other contract.

## Examples (hypothetical)

- A single-family homeowner signs a contract of $62,400.00: the Major Rebuild Agreement gate fits (single-family, $50,000.00 to $149,999.99), and one contract sum line of $62,400.00 is booked on the signing date.
- A landlord signs a contract of $31,000.00 for one apartment unit: the Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement gate fits.
